h: The Forest of Dean on your doorstep
p: Symonds Yat Rock sits right on the edge of the Forest of Dean, an ancient woodland with a long history of mining, timber and wildlife, and there's lots more to explore once you've had your fill of the view. Many visitors combine the Rock with a stop at Puzzlewood, near Coleford, a magical, moss-covered woodland of twisting paths, rocky gullies and wooden bridges that's been used as a filming location for big fantasy films and TV shows. Kids love it, and so do the grown-ups.

Nearby Clearwell Caves takes you underground into old iron mines that have been worked for thousands of years. It's a fascinating indoor option on a wet day, though it's cool down there, so bring a jumper even in summer.

Back down by the river, the Wye is popular for canoeing and kayaking, and there are hire companies in the valley if you fancy seeing the gorge from the water. Swimming in the river isn't something to try casually, though; currents can be strong and the water is colder than it looks.

The Wye Valley is a protected landscape, and the walk along the river towards Monmouth is a lovely one for a longer day. Back near Ross-on-Wye, the riverside meadows and the town's market house make a gentle end to the day.
